title: Chapter 1 – Introduction to Managerial Accounting (Objectives)
notes: Identify a manager's four primary responsibilities and discuss how managerial accounting aids in their fulfillment
Identify the differences between managerial accounting and financial accounting

flashcards.front: What are the four primary responsibilities of managers?
flashcards.back: Planning, Directing, Controlling, and Decision-making (evaluating alternatives using relevant info).

flashcards.front: How does managerial accounting support Planning?
flashcards.back: Provides forecasts, budgets, and what-if analyses to set goals and select strategies.

flashcards.front: How does managerial accounting support Directing?
flashcards.back: Supplies real-time reports and dashboards to coordinate day-to-day operations.

flashcards.front: How does managerial accounting support Controlling?
flashcards.back: Delivers variance analyses and performance reports to compare actuals vs. budget and take corrective action.

flashcards.front: How does managerial accounting support Decision-making?
flashcards.back: Offers relevant, timely, forward-looking information to choose among alternatives.

flashcards.front: Managerial vs Financial accounting: primary users?
flashcards.back: Managerial: internal managers; Financial: external users (investors, creditors, regulators).

flashcards.front: Managerial vs Financial accounting: focus and time horizon?
flashcards.back: Managerial: future-oriented, detailed segments; Financial: historical, company-wide aggregates.

flashcards.front: Managerial vs Financial accounting: rules and format?
flashcards.back: Managerial: not GAAP-mandated, flexible; Financial: GAAP/IFRS required, standardized.

flashcards.front: Managerial vs Financial accounting: frequency and timeliness?
flashcards.back: Managerial: frequent, as needed; Financial: periodic (quarterly/annual), less frequent.
Confidentiality, integrity, credibility; avoid conflicts of interest and ensure decision-useful reporting.
